text:
ari: Heads up — ACME procurement sent a pricing/packaging ask. They want per-department reserved capacity, hard monthly caps with auto-overage billing, priority routing for latency-sensitive endpoints, and a "add-on" for guaranteed burst credits. They want these in the term sheet for next week's ETR. thoughts?

jack: +1 urgent. Sales says they're close but this is a gating legal/finance item. They want a simple table in the contract: departments -> reserved tokens -> hard cap -> price.

molly: technical questions: priority routing implies a separate QoS tier in the serving layer. That is doable but needs routing policy, queueing, and billing signal. Estimate 6-8 sprint effort to be safe.

devon: finance view: hard caps + auto-overage ok, but we need clear rounding and billing windows. Also need per-dept invoicing or cost center tags in events. Otherwise messy for customers.

beth: legal: add-on language must be precise. "Guaranteed burst credits" needs definition (tokens, time window, non-cumulative?). We should avoid SLA promises on latency without SLO metrics and remediation clauses.

nina: product/design: console needs to show per-dept quotas, current usage, and ability to lift caps. Also UX for purchasing a burst pack. Low-fi mock would help negotiations.

ari: proposed product position options (quick sketches):
1) Offer "Reserved Tier" -- monthly committed tokens reserved per org/department + soft cap behavior (throttle + notify) as default. Add-on: "Burst Pack" (one-time purchase or monthly) gives N tokens that bypass soft throttle for short windows.
2) Offer "Guaranteed Priority" add-on -- routing into a priority queue with a latency SLO for a subset of endpoints/models. Requires capacity reservation or dynamic preemption.

jack: Sales prefers option 2 for ACME but they will accept 1 if cheaper. They asked for example term language and price delta.

molly: engineering constraints: priority queue needs kernel for preemption or separate fleet. If separate fleet -> reserved capacity product already exists (Dedicated) but customers expect hosted offering too. Work effort higher if hosted.

ari: minimum launch criteria I'm proposing before we present a firm price: billing integration for per-dept accounting, console UI for quota assignment, telemetry for per-dept usage and throttling events, documented overage billing rules, and legal-approved wording for burst packs.

devon: +1 -- also need invoice sample and GA telemetry retention window (30 days at minimum for negotiation).

beth: I'll draft conservative contract language for burst credits and priority routing disclaimers. Need input from eng for measurable SLO language.

molly: action items for eng: quick spike to evaluate priority routing implementation options (preemptive kernel vs separate fleet vs weights). 2w spike should give cost/ops estimate.

nina: I'll mock a single console screen with per-dept quotas and a purchase flow for Burst Pack — can have an initial mock in 3 days.

ari: timeline ask from sales: need a negotiation-ready offering by next Tues EOD. Given the spike, if engineering can't commit to priority routing we should push option 1 + clear upgrade path.

jack: agreed. I'll tell ACME we can ship Reserved Tier + Burst Pack as hosted offering this month pending legal/finance signoff, and that Guaranteed Priority is an enterprise add-on on roadmap with ETA TBD.

beth: drafting contract now. ping me when spike is done so I can add the SLO appendix if applicable.

molly: starting spike. will post findings in this thread and attach perf/cost roughs.

deploy-bot: deploy status: none triggered.

ari: thanks all — please drop quick replies if any objections. If no blockers, we'll proceed with spike + mock and reconvene Wed AM to finalize negotiation language. :thumbsup:

jack: no objections.

devon: fine from finance as long as rounding and billing windows are clear.

molly: no objections.

beth: no objections.

nina: good to go on design side.

ari: small config snippet for sales to show ACME (example only):
```\npricing:\n  reserved_tier:\n    dept_A: { committed_tokens: 50_000_000, price_monthly: "$6k" }\n    dept_B: { committed_tokens: 10_000_000, price_monthly: "$1.5k" }\n  burst_pack:\n    tokens: 5_000_000\n    price_one_time: "$2k"\n  overage: { per_token: "$0.00012", billing_window: "monthly", rounding: "1000" }\n```

ari: that'll be included as an illustrative example; final pricing table will come from finance. end.
